dedupe_keys.name: borrego springs microgrid blackstart and islanding with 100 renewable inverter based resources sdg e and nrel 2025

description: This case study is the September 2025 OSTI technical report Grid Resiliency with a 100% Renewable Microgrid, by San Diego Gas & Electric and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory, on the Borrego Springs Microgrid in San Diego County, a remote desert community served by a single transmission line. The project moved the microgrid from diesel-led operation to full renewable operation through equipment upgrades and a new microgrid controller that manages several battery storage systems. Field tests with synchrophasor monitoring and load-step evaluations confirmed that inverter-based resources can blackstart and island the microgrid in place of traditional generators. The work also validated a distributed energy resource management system controller that sets standard interfaces for adding further resources, and used hardware-in-the-loop and electromagnetic transient simulation to inform deployment and reduce field risk. Access: the report is free on OSTI; no licence is stated. Coverage is one community microgrid. Caveats: only the OSTI abstract was read, so measured values and controller settings are in the full report. It suits operations and control studies of islanded grids and resilience planning for remote communities, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
